question.bounded_question: Is Phase 18 safe to begin - is the research boundary immutable and recorded, is the accepted Phase 8 control exactly reconstructible, does a paper-plus-published-code method map resolve the Phase 17 interpretation, and are the evaluation questions frozen before any learner exists?
question.hypothesis_type: establishment, not measurement - no null/alternative applies because no experiment was run
question.predeclared_failure_interpretation: any unrecomputable Phase 8 identity, or an unavailable published source, stops Phase 18 and is reported as BLOCKED rather than worked around with the stale paper-only map

deviations: The published source was cloned read-only into the session scratchpad, outside the project tree. It was never executed, never imported and never added to the repository. Agent 1 instruction section 1 requires reading it and section 1 requires stopping if it is unavailable; it was available at exactly the pinned commit.

negative_and_contradictory_evidence: The 120-board pack used for the entire Phase 17 conclusion has a minimum detectable effect of 0.1379 EWR. Phase 17's flat and non-improving readings cannot be distinguished from a real effect inside roughly +/- 0.13. This weakens the Phase 17 negative result rather than supporting the Phase 18 hypothesis, and it is reported as such.
The unusual_procedural pack cannot be built from any existing asset, because the accepted Phase 8 corpus consumes the entire setup library. Phase 18's Claim B currently has no instrument.
One original Phase 8 gate (random EWR >= 0.950) is cleared by the accepted result by only 1.511 SE, so a faithful reproduction fails it about 6.5% of the time by luck alone.
The Phase 18 non-inferiority margins are predeclared judgments; no replicate Phase 8 run exists, so there is no measured run-to-run distribution to anchor them.

observed_fact: All 12 frozen Phase 8 identities recompute; the fresh C1 initialization rebuilds bit-exactly from seed 2026081302; all 28,000 corpus games re-hash clean at payload level.
The published source is available at exactly the pinned commit and its arrangement transformer at default config counts to 12,647,954 parameters, matching Table 23's 12.6 million.
The published code multiplies the stored entropy prediction by reg_norm = 10 before forming the residual; the paper's Table 19 and Eq. (1) are mutually inconsistent about the same symbol.
force_handedness defaults to True and post-generation reflection is applied; neither appears in the paper.
The published buffer aggregates repeated outcomes per setup by a running mean and zeroes its counters at each pool refresh.
The Phase 17 evaluator retry defect reproduces on execution.
The within-candidate correlation between the two Phase 17 evaluation lanes is 0.238, giving a paired difference sd of 0.5391 and an MDE of 0.1379 at n = 120.
The neutral_v1 profile samples uniformly over all 16 library families and the Phase 8 corpus draws all three library splits.
supported_inference: Gate G1 is reachable: the control's inputs and start point are exactly reconstructible.
Phase 17's setup implementation differed from the authors' in at least five material ways, so Phase 17 does not establish that the paper's setup method fails locally.
Phase 17's evaluation was underpowered for the effect sizes at issue, independently of the implementation differences.
No existing setup asset can serve as an unfamiliar-opponent stratum.
plausible_but_untested: That the entropy-unit defect is the dominant cause of the Phase 17 setup result. The uncentered term is real and large, but nothing here measures its contribution against the m=1 outcome variance or the 32-episode batch.
That correcting all five items produces a setup policy that beats the fixed library. That is Gate G3's question and is not answered.
claim_not_supported: That Phase 18's corrections will work. Nothing was trained.
That Phase 17's negative result was caused by any specific one of the five differences.
That the Phase 8 control will reproduce. It was not run.
